name: Brazilian Sign Language
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Sign language (Libras); no published description of word stress found; spoken-language stress category not applicable.

new_statements.quote: Dentre os dados analisados foram constatados a presença de sinais: Com mais de duas sílabas; Predominantemente sensíveis ao peso silábico; Predominantemente, com sílaba tônica na penúltima sílaba; Com grande probidade de a proeminência ser por intensidade. Ao encontrarmos essas características na Libras, percebemos que, assim como acontece no PB, na Libras o acento não é totalmente livre, por conter restrições nas possibilidades de realização, antepenúltima, penúltima e última sílaba do sinal fonológico. Contudo podemos intuir que seja razoavelmente previsível, pois, predominantemente, recai na penúltima sílaba.
new_statements.translation: Among the data analysed we found signs: with more than two syllables; predominantly sensitive to syllable weight; predominantly with the tonic syllable on the penultimate syllable; with a high likelihood that prominence is by intensity. Finding these characteristics in Libras, we see that, as in Brazilian Portuguese, stress in Libras is not totally free, since it is restricted in where it can be realised: antepenultimate, penultimate and final syllable of the phonological sign. However, we may infer that it is reasonably predictable, since it predominantly falls on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Passos, Alessandra Figueiredo Kraus. 2018. Fonética e fonologia da Libras: o acento. Dissertação (Mestrado em Linguística), Programa de Pós-Graduação em Linguística, Universidade do Estado de Mato Grosso (UNEMAT), Cáceres-MT. 98 f.
new_statements.locator: Considerações Finais, p. 91 (p. 93); see also p. 92 and Resumo p. [vii]
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (98 pp., text present; companion). QUOTE: extracted text of p. 93 (printed p. 91, 'Considerações Finais') reproduces the reported passage word for word: 'Dentre os dados analisados foram constatados a presença de sinais: / Com mais de duas sílabas; / Predominantemente sensíveis ao peso silábico; / Predominantemente, com sílaba tônica na penúltima sílaba; / Com grande probidade de a proeminência ser por intensidade. / Ao encontrarmos essas características na Libras.. o acento não é totalmente livre, por conter restrições nas possibilidades de realização, antepenúltima, penúltima e última sílaba do sinal fonológico. Contudo podemos intuir que seja razoavelmente previsível, pois,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Author's claim: Libras signs ('phonological signs') can be polysyllabic (syllable nucleus = place of articulation, after Aguiar 2013); the prominent syllable is attracted by syllable weight (a filled 'coda' = movement/non-manual), lies within a final three-syllable window and is most often the penult; prominence is realised by intensity, duration or height in signing space, and because syllables can be simultaneous the accent may fall on a whole sign rather than one syllable. Contrast: for ASL, Wilbur 1999 (summarised by Passos pp. 67-69) says lexical stress is trivially predictable/leftmost because most signs are monosyllabic.
new_statements.exceptions: Some signs analysed as proparoxytone (FINO, SORTE, BOMBA, p. 85) and some compounds with final (oxytone) prominence after resyllabification (p. 79); in signs with simultaneous syllables (e.g. TEATRO, ALEGRAR) 'o acento recai no sinal' rather than on a syllable (pp. 82, 85).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form dictionary signs (Novo Deit-Libras drawings/descriptions), 29 items, qualitative; domain is the author's 'sinal fonológico' (phonological word analogue), including compounds. Visual-gestural modality: 'stress' = visual prominence, not acoustic.
new_statements.identity_note: Libras in general (no dialect); Passos 2018 analyses citation-form signs drawn from the Novo Deit-Libras dictionary (Capovilla & Raphael), i.e. the São Paulo-based standard lexicon. NOTE: this is a sign language; 'syllable' and 'stress' here are the author's visual-gestural analogues (syllable nucleus = place of articulation, following Aguiar 2013), not acoustic stress. The file saved in the same folder is NOT Libras (Kithãulhu, Nambikwaran) and was downloaded incidentally.

new_statements.quote: [p. 222] Por fim, as instâncias de turnos simples me permitiram levantar ainda uma hipótese sobre a manifestação formal do acento enfático na libras. [...] No que se refere às modulações do sinal manual, nota-se uma longa preparação, uma manutenção da suspensão pré-golpe por quatro frames, seguida de um rápido deslocamento do golpe no espaço. [p. 254] a modulação do sinal manual [preparação mais longa + suspensão pré-golpe + golpe mais rápido e intenso], identificada na análise de turnos simples, foi constatada numa frase diferenciando um dentre três sinais fonologicamente idênticos, o sinal modulado estando relacionado justamente à introdução da informação nova no contexto em questão.
new_statements.translation: [p. 222] Finally, the instances of simple turns also allowed me to raise a hypothesis about the formal manifestation of emphatic accent in Libras. [...] As for the modulations of the manual sign, one notes a long preparation, a holding of the pre-stroke hold for four frames, followed by a rapid displacement of the stroke in space. [p. 254] the modulation of the manual sign [longer preparation + pre-stroke hold + faster and more intense stroke], identified in the analysis of simple turns, was found in a phrase differentiating one of three phonologically identical signs, the modulated sign being related precisely to the introduction of the new information in the context in question.
new_statements.citation: Leite, Tarcísio de Arantes. 2008. A segmentação da língua de sinais brasileira (libras): um estudo lingüístico descritivo a partir da conversação espontânea entre surdos. Tese (Doutorado), FFLCH, Universidade de São Paulo.
new_statements.locator: §7.3.5 'Acento enfático', p. 222; hypothesis restated p. 245 and p. 254 (§7.5); Tabela 6 'Marcas formais prosódicas de acentuação na libras', p. 257; also p. 212 and p. 233
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened (the PDF's metadata: Leite, USP 2008, 280 pp., text; printed page number = PDF page, footer '222' on p. 222). p. 222, §7.3.5 'Acento enfático': both quoted sentences are there verbatim ('Por fim, as instâncias de turnos simples me permitiram levantar ainda uma hipótese sobre a manifestação formal do acento enfático na libras.'.. 'No que se refere às modulações do sinal manual, nota-se uma longa preparação, uma manutenção da suspensão pré-golpe por quatro frames, seguida de um rápido deslocamento do golpe no espaço.'); the [..] elides one sentence about raised eyebrows and head projection on IGUAL. p. 254 (§7.5 summary): the second quote is verbatim. Tabela 6 on p. 257 is as desc…
new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with, but on a different level than, the existing Passos 2018 statement. Passos places stress predominantly on the penultimate syllable of a sign, weight-sensitively, with intensity as the likely cue; Leite says nothing about the position of stress within a sign and instead describes emphatic/phrasal accent on whole signs within intonation units (cue: faster, more intense stroke after a longer preparation and pre-stroke hold, plus gaze shifts). The 'more intense stroke' cue is consonant with Passos's intensity-based prominence. Nothing here contradicts Passos; it adds the phrase-level domain and boundary cues (final lengthening, initial acceleration).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Leite treats 'acento' only as emphatic/informational prominence of a whole sign inside an intonation unit (UE), never as a position inside a sign. Manual cue (Tabela 6, p. 257): longer preparation, then a pre-stroke hold, then a faster and longer/more intense stroke, marking the informationally salient item of the UE (new information, contrasted item); non-manual cue: brief gaze shifts from a stable pattern to discrete points during the UE. Also describes final lengthening (§7.3.1, p. 212 ff., held post-stroke hold / extra repetitions, in phrase-final signs) and initial acceleration (§7.3.2, p. 216, fewer repetitions in phrase-initial signs) as intonation-unit boundary cues. The thesis explicitly frames all of this as hypotheses from a small conversational corpus (p. 222-223, 254-255).
new_statements.secondary_stress: none stated; the accent hypotheses are graded (p. 245: the second instance of PREFERIR shows a 'less salient' accent with a shorter pre-stroke hold and more moderate stroke), but no primary/secondary distinction is proposed
new_statements.exceptions: none; the author stresses the tentative, single-instance basis of the emphatic-accent hypothesis (p. 212, 222) and calls for perception experiments (fn. 173, p. 222)
new_statements.identity_note: Both works describe Libras as used in São Paulo: Leite's corpus is spontaneous conversation among deaf signers recorded at USP; Xavier's data come from the Capovilla & Raphael (2001) dictionary (São Paulo). Neither claims a regional variety, and neither describes another language.)

sources.locator: Considerações Finais, p. 91 (p. 93); see also p. 92 and Resumo p. [vii]
sources.note: Whole thesis is on stress in Libras. Using 29 signs from the Novo Deit-Libras dictionary and Aguiar's (2013) syllable model (place of articulation = nucleus), concludes (p. 91) that Libras has stress; signs can have more than two syllables; stress is predominantly weight-sensitive, restricted to antepenult/penult/final of the 'phonological sign', predominantly penultimate, realised mainly by intensity (also duration, height); because of modality it may fall on a whole sign rather than a syllable. Summarises Wilbur 1999 (ASL lexical stress leftmost/predictable, most signs monosyllabic) on pp.…
